title: 1974: Mr. McVea's band and the priests who threw dollars
summary: Howard describes Isaac McVea as a banjo player, a fine man to work for, though priests once threw dollars at his head.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: You talk about Jack's father. Now Jack's

father, he had this band, you know, and Mac -- Mr. McVea, all of us called him Mr. McVea, he was kind of a -- you know, a Thomas with a banjo. But he was a fine man to work for. He wouldn't let nobody do nothing to you, only he let some priests one-time throw dollars at me and try to hit me in the head with a dollar, up in Santa Barbara. You remember that?
I remember you told me that once.
Did I tell you that? How long ago has that been?
Oh, I don't remember, but I remember you telling me one time about the priests and the dollars.

(Unintelligible) But I mean when you let things like that go it's not too good, you know. But other than that Mr. McVea was a pretty nice man. And he had -- he had -- well, he didn't have no style of playing or anything like that.
No. He'd just pick a banjo, you know. But he could play a pretty good strong lead when he got on it and got to going on it, it was good, and that was all that was necessary.
He seemed to get quite a few jobs, is that right?
